title.narrative: Chhattisgarh Public Financial Management and Accountability Program

description.narrative: The objective of the Chhattisgarh Public Financial Management and Accountability Program Project is to: improve accountability in the management of public finances; strengthen revenue administration; and improve efficiency in delivery of benefits in selected schemes, in the state of Chhattisgarh. India is among the world's fastest growing economies and has made remarkable progress in poverty reduction and human development. Wide-ranging and ongoing macroeconomic, fiscal, tax and business environment reforms have enabled rapid growth. Already the third largest economy in the world in purchasing parity terms, the country is expected to grow at over 7 percent a year in coming years. Over the past thirty years, per capita incomes quadrupled, poverty retreated, illiteracy rates dropped, and health-related statistics improved. India's extreme poverty rate halved from 46 percent to 21 percent in the two decades up to 2011. While growth in India has been impressive, it needs to be equally shared; India faces social, institutional and policy challenges. To meet the development goals, India needs to adapt its institutions to improve public sector performance and deliver services effectively to its citizens. Improvements in service delivery requires improvements in accountability, efficiency, and effectiveness along the chain from inputs to outcomes. Competition between states is part of a new dynamic to incentivize change, using funding to hold states accountable for progress based upon their own priorities. India has a federal, three-tier structure of Government comprising the national or Union level; states; and districts. The fiscal relationship between the Union and the States is reflected in revenue sharing, devolution of central taxes and assistance in the form of grants. Recent policy level changes at the Union level, have increased the share of Union resources devolved to the states, reduced the share of resources through tied transfers under Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) and introduced a Goods and Service Tax (GST) that is expected to contribute to growth in state revenues. In the medium term, increases in untied resources are expected to result in states managing nearly 60 percent of total public expenditure. The move toward increased expenditure flexibility for states presents both an opportunity and challenge. The opportunity lies in the greater freedom to align local development needs and priorities with the resources available. The challenge lies in the development of robust public financial management systems that can allocate and deliver resources in line with policy priorities.

The objective of the program is to: improve accountability in the management of public finances; strengthen revenue administration; and improve efficiency in delivery of benefits in selected schemes, in the state of Chhattisgarh.

condition.narrative: Advance: The Borrower may withdraw an amount not to exceed two million Dollars ($ 2,000,000) as an advance; provided, however,that if the DLRs in the opinion of the Bank, [is/are] not achieved (or only partially achieved) by the Closing Date, the Borrowershall refund such advance to the Bank promptly upon notice thereof by the Bank. Except as otherwise agreed with the Borrower, theBank shall cancel the amount so refunded. Any further withdrawals requested as an advance under any Category shall be permittedonly on such terms and conditions as the Bank shall specify by notice to the Borrower.

DLI Verification: By no later than 3 (three) months after the Effective Date: (a) hire, and thereafter maintain throughout Programimplementation, an Independent Verification Agency (IVA) to verify the fulfillment of the Disbursement Linked Results in accordancewith terms of reference agreed with the Bank; (b) Undertake, at least annually, in view of the submission of a withdrawalapplication, a verification process, in accordance with the terms of reference agreed with the Bank, to certify the fulfillment ofthe DLRs; and (c) furnish to the Bank corresponding verification report(s), in form and substance agreed with the Bank.

Mid-term Review: The Borrower, together with Chhattisgarh Program implementing Entity shall jointly with the Bank carry out one(1) mid-term review of the Program to assess the status of the Program Implementation, as measured against the indicators andresults framework agreed with the Bank and the legal covenants included/referred to in this Agreement and/or the Program Agreement,and shall incorporate the findings of such review into the Program design for the subsequent years and take all such measuresnecessary for the efficient completion of the Program based on the recommendations of the review and the Bank's views on thematter.

Personal Data: Ensure that the Program's activities involving collection, storage, usage, and/or processing of Personal Data arecarried out with due regard to the Borrower's existing legal framework and appropriate international data protection and privacystandards and practices.

Program Institutions: The Borrower shall cause Chhattisgarh to maintain, throughout the period of implementation of the Program(a) a Program Steering Committee with a mandate and composition agreed with the Bank; (b) a state Program Management Unit withinthe Directorate of Institutional Finance, with functions, resources agreed with the Bank; and (c) a state Fiscal Cell within theFinance Department, with functions, resources agreed with the Bank.

title.narrative: IR indicator 4.2 Enhancement of Tax Analytics, Information and Audit Systems

baseline.value: Currently VAT system is fully computerized and inhouse MIS & Analytical reports are based on VAT computerized database. GST analytics is rudimentary as the MIS is not fully developed and analytics module is yet to be rolled out. No specialized audit mechanisms in place.

target.value: Functional Tax analytics platform available for analysis of GST tax returns, monitoring fraud, return filing status etc. integrated with existing VAT data. Audit framework and systems created and supported by Analytics platform

comment.narrative: For FY25-26, the State has provisioned Rs. 40 crores for enhancing the Business Intelligence Unit at CTD.

actual.value: he Commercial Tax Department migrated to National Informatics Centre (NIC) Karnataka's GST Prime for tax analytics supplemented by the GSTN's Business Intelligence and Fraud Analytics platform. In addition, a GST related data lake was created blending GST returns and third-party information for detection of potential non-compliance. The assistance enabled detection of GST related tax fraud and excess IT credit through mass audit of returns identifying discrepancy. Data on GST collection through this exercise is awaited.

title.narrative: IR Indicator 1.3: Structured training of GoCG staff in Public Financial Management and Public Procurement

baseline.value: Existing Accounts Training Schools (ATSs) have inadequate institutional capacity and infrastructure to train GoCG's large pool of staff on PFM and Public Procurement. The total number of officers in the above-mentioned cadre are 10 443 including 10% female staff.

target.value: At least 3,000 government staff, including 10% female staff trained in Public Financial Management and Public Procurement

comment.narrative: Target achieved

actual.value: During the Program tenure 966 personnel of the Finance Department, 1908 officers of the Commercial Tax Department and 143 staff of the Chhattisgarh State Audit Directorate were trained. Over all 3017 staff were trained .

title.narrative: PDO Indicator 1: Complete and timely State financial reports available In public domain

baseline.value: Financial reports generated from e-kosh incomplete as expenditures of Public Works and Forest Divisions, Treasury (PAO) and RES are not reported.

target.value: Complete and timely State financial reports available in public domain.

comment.narrative: Achieved; The interfaces and modules enabled the transition of e-Kosh from a core treasury system to a more comprehensive Financial Management Information System (FMIS). It enabled a 360-degree view of financial transactions to budget executing officers and the government system's decision makers.

actual.value: Interoperability of the treasury system (e-Kosh) with key external and internal platforms, including the Reserve Bank of India's e-Kuber, the e-Government procurement system (e-GP), and the e-payments and contract management systems of five Works Departments (e-Works) enabled. Additionally, an interface between e-Kosh and the State Accountant General's software has been operationalized, allowing AG office staff to securely access and review accounts and vouchers from all 34 Treasuries, thereby enhancing audit transparency and oversight.

target.value: Audits completed in at least 10,500 units for the five period from FY17-18 to FY21-22

comment.narrative: The intended result of reduction in back log of audit of local bodies has been achieved albeit for the four years (FY 2021-2023-24) Instead of the originally targeted 5 years (FY 2017-18 to FY 2021-22) as required as per the revised DLI..

actual.value: Audit of more than 10,500 rural local bodies (Gram Panchayats) were completed for each of the financial years 2020-21 to 2023-24 by the Directorate of Chhattisgarh State Audit using the Audit Online application.

title.narrative: IR Indicator 1.2: Macro-fiscal model developed under a Medium Term Fiscal Framework (MTFF) for forecasting of long-term macro-economic and fiscal indicators

baseline.value: MTFF prepared as part of annual budget exercise, but lacks rigor and clear statement of underlying technical assumptions

target.value: Macro-fiscal model developed under a Medium Term Fiscal Framework (MTFF) for forecasting of long-term macro-economic and fiscal indicators. Forecasts generated through the MTFF used to prepare the statements to meet the requirements of the State FRBM Act, and for estimating the expenditure ceiling of the budget.

comment.narrative: The user manual and training curriculum on the model has been prepared and approved

actual.value: The MTFF model was developed by the State customizing the FSA tool of the World Bank. This tool was used to generate fiscal disclosures under the State FRBM Act for the next three financial years and for estimating the overall expenditure ceiling as part of budget exercise of FY 2024-25 and 2025-26. The user manual and training curriculum on the model has been prepared and approved

title.narrative: IR Indicator 1.1: Development and implementation of new Public Investment Management Framework for capital investment projects

baseline.value: Project Formulation and Implementation Committee headed by Chief Secretary approves all public investment proposals above Rs. 50 crores; the process however requires rigor and technical cost benefit analysis.

target.value: Appraisal of at least 10% of all capital investment projects in selected two departments, conducted using the new PIM Framework.

comment.narrative: The policy is expected to be approved soon.

actual.value: Chhattisgarh is the first Indian States to prepare a comprehensive diagnostic gap analysis and a PIM policy which is serving as a blueprint for other States like Punjab and Assam seeking to develop PIM policies. However, the competent authority in GoCG is yet to approve the PIM policy document and therefore, implementation of the policy in appraisal of capital investment projects in selected two departments is not achieved at program closure.

target.value: Finance Budget and Accounting Management module rolled out and fully operational across 14 Nagar Nigams, 43 Nagar Palikas and 112 Nagar Panchayats.

comment.narrative: Target achieved

actual.value: The Finance Budget and Accounting Management Module of the ERP solution has been rolled out and is operational across 14 Nagar Nigams, 43 Nagar Palikas and 112 Nagar Panchayats. For FY25-26, the State has provisioned Rs. 10 crores for development of an integrated dashboard for urban Administration (ULBs).

title.narrative: PDO Indicator 5: Universal use of DBT for validated baseline of beneficiaries in selected schemes

baseline.value: Total number of beneficiaries covered under the five selected schemes are 883,448, of which 0% are DBT compliant

target.value: Use of DBT in 90% of validated baseline of beneficiaries in the shortlisted schemes

comment.narrative: Upon additional validation against the IPeG social registry, which is presently limited to PDS beneficiary database, the number of beneficiaries further reduced. Thereafter, the labor department carried out field level verification of beneficiaries and transferred benefits digitally.

actual.value: Of the total number of 10,16,546 beneficiaries in the department records, the validation processes with data exchange platform and the scheme protocols pared down the number to 214,307 with approx. 80% beneficiaries eliminated

title.narrative: IR Indicator 4.1: Institutional performance of CTD enhanced, through training of staff

baseline.value: Non-filers of GST return are 28% percentage of active dealers: no proper training schedule/plan in place.

target.value: Decline in GST tax return non-filers to 15% of active dealers; training schedule plan created

comment.narrative: To strengthen institutional capacity, CTD renovated its IT infrastructure purchasing 630 desktop computers, 45 laptops, 60 scanners, and 500 printers.

actual.value: GST tax return non-filers currently average less than 10 percent, a significant improvement compared to the baseline.
